title: Correct acceleration value
description: Essential: The response must state the correct acceleration as 0.1 m/s².

title: Correct average velocity
description: Essential: The response must state the correct average velocity for the first 6 seconds as 2.55 m/s.

title: Apply displacement difference formula
description: Important: The solution must correctly use the formula for the difference in displacements in two given seconds (e.g., x_7 - x_3 = 4aT²) to find acceleration.

title: Find initial velocity correctly
description: Important: The solution must correctly calculate the initial velocity (v0 ≈ 2.25 m/s) using the displacement in a specific second and the known acceleration.

title: Calculate final velocity at t=6s
description: Important: The solution must correctly compute the velocity at t=6 seconds (v6 = 2.85 m/s) using v = v0 + at.

title: Use correct average velocity formula
description: Important: For uniform acceleration, the solution must correctly apply the average velocity formula ( (v_initial + v_final)/2 ) over the first 6 seconds.

title: Misinterpret 'n-th second' displacement
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly treats the displacement in the 'n-th second' as the total displacement after n seconds.

title: Sign or unit error
description: Pitfall: Penalize significant sign errors in kinematic equations or omission/incorrect use of units (m/s, m/s²) in final answers.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: Award credit if the student explicitly checks unit consistency in their calculations.
